ok-oklahoma-2026-treasurer-thompson-jess.name: Jessica Thompson
ok-oklahoma-2026-treasurer-thompson-jess.bio: Real estate broker and owner of CityBurb Homes and board chair of the Neighborhood Alliance of Central Oklahoma.

positions.stance: Will work to make county finances clearer, easier to understand and more accessible to all taxpayers.
Supports an independent audit of the Oklahoma County Treasurer's Office to ensure it operates responsibly, ethically and effectively.
Will bring "a steady, responsible approach to protecting public dollars."
Will work with the District Attorney and other county officials to address legal compliance issues and ensure the office follows the law.
Wants to bring the Treasurer's Office "into the 21st century" by improving public access, communication and user-friendliness.

ut-salt-lake-2026-council-at-large-a-and.name: Kathleen Anderson
ut-salt-lake-2026-council-at-large-a-and.bio: Small business owner and community leader who has lived in Salt Lake County for 36 years.

positions.stance: Says "taxes keep rising" and pledges respect for taxpayers and honest budgeting at County Hall.
Calls for safer parks and public spaces, citing "drugs, crime, trash, vandalism and disorder."
Supports local business, saying small businesses "are treated like collateral damage."
Criticizes "road projects that drag on too long" and calls for county government that works.
Wants to restore county child care and senior services, advocate for affordable housing, and support property tax relief for vulnerable populations.
Opposes the Little Cottonwood Canyon gondola project and supports water conservation and improved air quality.
Opposes the proposed ICE detention facility in the county and supports public safety training, school route safety and mental health programs.
Believes "it is possible to reform the criminal justice system without compromising public safety."
Supports a justice system that addresses root causes of issues like addiction, domestic violence, and mental health.
"Public safety means holding offenders accountable, supporting victims, and building a justice system that works for every community."
Cites Mental Health Court, Veterans Court and pre-filing diversion as ways to reduce repeat offenses and get people treatment instead of incarceration.

ut-salt-lake-2026-district-attorney-davi.name: Kent Davis
ut-salt-lake-2026-district-attorney-davi.bio: Former Salt Lake County Deputy District Attorney and public defender; Army combat veteran and corporate counsel at Woodbury Corporation.

positions.stance: Supports consistent screening so similar cases receive similar treatment, with a documented reason for each declination.
Would record plea terms, rationale and supervisor approval, and use data to manage prosecutor caseloads.
Will publish indicators of case processing, workloads, screening and outcomes on a public dashboard.
Supports clear admission criteria focused on public safety and drivers like drug dependency and mental health, with tracked outcomes.

ut-salt-lake-2026-auditor-cloward-ali.name: Ali Cloward
ut-salt-lake-2026-auditor-cloward-ali.bio: Certified Internal Auditor with over 15 years of auditing experience, working at a national firm.

positions.stance: "The government shouldn't waste a single taxpayer dollar"; wants the county to get the most out of every dollar it spends.
Pledges honesty and consistency, giving residents "the straight truth, even when it's not the easy answer."
Committed to transparency that puts the facts in front of residents so they can hold their government accountable.

ut-salt-lake-2026-clerk-chapman-lannie.name: Lannie Chapman
ut-salt-lake-2026-clerk-chapman-lannie.bio: Salt Lake County Clerk since 2023; former Chief Deputy Clerk and Salt Lake County Deputy District Attorney.

positions.stance: Committed to continuing high voter turnout through vote-by-mail, described as a "safe, effective, and accessible method of voting."
Will ensure "public offices remain in the hands of public servants" for elections, passports and marriage licenses.
Has worked with Homeland Security, Unified Police and the Sheriff's office on election safety and security measures.

ut-salt-lake-2026-sheriff-manwaring-shan.name: Shane Manwaring
ut-salt-lake-2026-sheriff-manwaring-shan.bio: Law enforcement leader with the Unified Police Department and a Colonel in the Utah Army National Guard.

positions.stance: Says rule of law must be enforced consistently and policies that weaken consequences for repeat offenders will be rejected.
Will lead with integrity and clear public communication to rebuild confidence in the Sheriff's Office.
Supports equal treatment under the law and strengthening jail operations for safety, compliance and professional management.

ut-salt-lake-2026-sheriff-rivera-rosie.name: Rosie Rivera
ut-salt-lake-2026-sheriff-rivera-rosie.bio: Salt Lake County Sheriff with a 32-year law enforcement career.

positions.stance: Calls transparency "essential to building trust in law enforcement" and pledges to hold her team to the highest standard.
Focuses on preventing crime, supporting victims, holding offenders accountable, and community policing.
Prioritizes mental health care, substance use treatment and supervised programs, saying accountability "can take many forms outside of incarceration."

nv-clark-2026-assessor-joe-judy.name: Judy Joe
nv-clark-2026-assessor-joe-judy.bio: Clark County homeowner and taxpayer advocate with over 10 years in federal compliance and work as a volunteer mediator.

positions.stance: Says assessments should reflect what homes are really worth and residents deserve to know where their taxes go.
"Seniors who've paid off their homes and veterans who served shouldn't be taxed out of them."
Wants every eligible family to get the 3% property tax cap, "not the 8%."
Wants an office that answers clearly and honestly, "in the languages this county actually speaks."

nv-clark-2026-assessor-washington-tamick.name: Tamicka N. Washington
nv-clark-2026-assessor-washington-tamick.bio: Longtime employee of the Clark County Assessor's Office.

positions.stance: Focuses on ensuring property assessment accuracy in the Assessor's Office.
Aims to enhance public transparency in the Assessor's Office.
Supports "implementing fair tax policies that protect our community's future."

nv-clark-2026-clerk-goya-lynn.name: Lynn Marie Goya
nv-clark-2026-clerk-goya-lynn.bio: Clark County Clerk, running for a fourth term.

nv-clark-2026-clerk-shaw-howell.name: Howell Shaw
nv-clark-2026-clerk-shaw-howell.bio: Henderson-based Stanford-trained product designer, educator, entrepreneur and pastor.

positions.stance: Proposes an opt-in anniversary program with perks and keepsakes to bring married couples back to Las Vegas.
Proposes a secure online application and hotel kiosks for instant, identity-verified marriage licenses at any hour.
Proposes an online filing tool with e-signature and immediate digital certificates for fictitious firm names.
Supports open online record search, published fee schedules, live wait times and public performance dashboards.
Supports disciplined operations and "responsible automation that cut waste without cutting service."

nv-clark-2026-recorder-flanagan-tanya.name: Tanya Flanagan
nv-clark-2026-recorder-flanagan-tanya.bio: Clark County government employee for more than 23 years, currently in a leadership role in the Clark County Recorder's Office.

positions.stance: Supports strengthening the Recorder's Office technology to improve efficiency, document security and online access.
Focuses on ensuring the Recorder's Office runs efficiently with disciplined management and high public service standards.
Wants better communication and service delivery for title companies, lenders and legal professionals who rely on the office.

nv-clark-2026-recorder-young-bill.name: Bill Young
nv-clark-2026-recorder-young-bill.bio: Retired police detective, business owner and certified mediator.

positions.stance: Will lobby the Nevada Legislature for laws to prevent deed fraud and will check records for deed flaws and notify owners.
Will lobby for stronger laws to protect homeowners, saying "no squatter should have any right to anyone's home."
Wants a mandatory service model like the help customers get at Home Depot or Lowe's.
Supports restoring Friday service at the Recorder's Office, or at least Friday phone support.

nv-clark-2026-treasurer-diaz-j.name: J. "Ken" Diaz
nv-clark-2026-treasurer-diaz-j.bio: Clark County Treasurer since 2022, certified public accountant, and Air Force veteran.

nv-clark-2026-treasurer-tracy-mitchell.name: Mitchell T. Tracy
nv-clark-2026-treasurer-tracy-mitchell.bio: Accounting and finance professional with over 22 years of experience, former business owner, and military reserve veteran.

positions.stance: "I will audit Clark County government for fraud, abuse, and waste."
Pledges to reduce credit and debit card fees.
Committed to safeguarding taxpayer dollars and transparent, responsible financial management for Clark County.
Supports law and order, all law enforcement and the military, and defending the U.S. Constitution.
Advocates for parents' rights and "less government intrusion into citizens' daily lives."

nv-clark-2026-pubadmin-itkin-goodman-ste.name: Stephanie Itkin-Goodman
nv-clark-2026-pubadmin-itkin-goodman-ste.bio: Nevada Deputy Attorney General and former Assistant District Attorney.

positions.stance: Says the office requires legal judgment and that, as a licensed attorney, she can protect estates from day one.
Supports clear standards, consistent communication with families and improved processes so estates are handled promptly.
Says every estate, regardless of size, must be handled with strict accounting, clear procedures and careful oversight.
Believes the office should ultimately be a professional career position led by qualified public servants rather than a political office.

ca-los-angeles-2026-sheriff-luna-robert.name: Robert G. Luna
ca-los-angeles-2026-sheriff-luna-robert.bio: Los Angeles County Sheriff since 2022; former Long Beach Chief of Police.

positions.stance: Says reducing crime requires holding habitual offenders accountable plus prevention through community engagement and social services.
Cites reforms including an Office of Constitutional Policing, a ban on law enforcement gangs, and public data dashboards.
Supports increased budgeted positions, academy classes and long overdue equipment and technology upgrades.
Dedicated to supporting deputies' wellbeing with mental health care, peer counseling and reducing stigma around seeking help.
Campaigned for Measure A and Proposition 1 and supports LASD's Homeless Outreach Services Teams.

ca-los-angeles-2026-sheriff-villanueva-a.name: Alex Villanueva
ca-los-angeles-2026-sheriff-villanueva-a.bio: Former Los Angeles County Sheriff (elected 2018) and 36-year veteran of the Sheriff's Department; military veteran.

ca-los-angeles-2026-mayor-raman-nithya.name: Nithya Raman
ca-los-angeles-2026-mayor-raman-nithya.bio: Los Angeles City Councilmember for District 4 and urban planner.

positions.stance: Pledges to "make sure Angelenos have a home they can afford."
Will "fix the city": fill potholes, pave roads, plant trees, turn on streetlights, and put parks near residents.
Will protect Angelenos "from ICE, from harassing landlords, from unsafe streets, from fires and natural disasters" and ensure 911 response.
Pledges to "end the pay-to-play politics that have dominated the city for decades."
Will make it easier to start and run a business, support restaurants and bars, and "bring the Hollywood jobs back home."
Will build more housing faster by making City Hall easier to work with and using public land and public financing.
Will lower everyday costs, revive downtown, and support film and TV and small businesses that create good jobs.
Will build a system that prevents crime, intervenes swiftly, and gives justice-impacted people second chances to limit recidivism.
Will build a City-run homelessness system that gets people indoors, treats health needs, and helps them rebuild independent lives.
Will build on her Executive Directives and the Sanctuary City Ordinance with policies supporting immigrant communities.

ca-los-angeles-2026-cityattorney-mckinne.name: John McKinney
ca-los-angeles-2026-cityattorney-mckinne.bio: Prosecutor for nearly three decades; Bureau Director of Specialized Prosecutions in the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office.

positions.stance: Will restore the Neighborhood Prosecutor Program, placing prosecutors in communities to address nuisance properties, illegal dumping and neighborhood crime.
Will focus on repeat offenders, retail theft, illegal firearms possession, street racing and open-air drug markets.
Says tenants deserve safe housing and legal protections, while property owners deserve clear rules and consistent enforcement.
Says "every worker deserves dignity, fairness, and protection under the law," citing wage theft and unsafe conditions.
Supports keeping sidewalks passable and addressing dangerous encampments while helping people access housing, treatment and support.
